land.text: the Isthmus of Panama, the Panama Department of Colombia: 'the 1886 constitution of the modern Republic of Colombia created a new Panama Department'; Panama 'proclaimed its independence' from Colombia in November 1903

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first Panama shape begins in 1905; the page dates the separation 3 November 1903 (infobox 'from Republic of Colombia: November 3, 1903'). The future Canal Zone was inside the country until the May 1904 turnover.

capitals.name: Panama City
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Panama City 8°58′N 79°32′W'. The page does not date the seat of government separately from the 1903 independence.

correction.text: Panama at independence on 3 November 1903, still holding the land of the future Canal Zone: the zone 'was created on November 18, 1903, from the territory of Panama' and 'formally turned over by Panama on May 4, 1904' (the shape of Cliopatria's 2000 Panama, which includes it)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1903: Cliopatria's first Panama shape begins in 1905. At one-year resolution the Zone is Panama's in 1903 (turnover 4 May 1904) and America's from 1904, so the 1903 shape includes it.

correction.text: shape unchanged, but it holds for 1904-1978 only: Panama without the Canal Zone, from the formal turnover of 4 May 1904 until the Zone 'ceased to exist on October 1, 1979'; Cliopatria keeps the Zone out until 1999

keyframe_review.note: 82,295 km2 against the infobox's 75,417 km2 (ratio 1.09; the body text gives 74,177.3 km2): within the factor of two. The Zone (5 cells, about 1,285 km2) is the only difference from the 2000 shape; the page's 1,430 km2 agrees. The years change, not the outline: 1904-1978.

correction.text: Panama with the former Canal Zone, back under its jurisdiction from 1 October 1979; the Canal itself, 35 defence enclaves and the rest stayed American or joint until 'Just after noon local time on December 31, 1999'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria returns the Zone only in 2000. The page has the Zone abolished on 1 October 1979 and the surrounding territory 'returned first, in 1979' (Panama page); the enclaves cannot be drawn separately at this resolution, so the 2000 outline is used from 1979.
83,580 km2 against the infobox's 75,417 km2 (ratio 1.11): within the factor of two (presumably the grid's coastal margin). Valid from 1979 on the pages, not from 2000 (see republic-of-panama_1979).
Same outline as 2000-2023; the page records no border change after the 1999 handover.

region.text: Panama, which 'proclaimed its independence' in November 1903

ledger.note: 1903: Panama proclaims its independence from Colombia on 3 November. 'In November 1903, Panama, tacitly supported by the United States, proclaimed its independence'; infobox 'from Republic of Colombia: November 3, 1903'. The page names the country, not a boundary; the Zone is still inside it at this date.

region.text: the Panama Canal Zone, 'five miles (8 km) on each side of the centerline', 553 sq mi (1,430 km2)

ledger.note: 1904: Panama turns the Canal Zone over to the United States on 4 May. 'The Panama Canal Zone was created on November 18, 1903, from the territory of Panama' under the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty and 'the Canal Zone was formally turned over by Panama on May 4, 1904'; the Panama page: the treaty gave the US rights 'as if it were sovereign' in a zone roughly 16 km wide.

region.text: the Panama Canal Zone, 'five miles (8 km) on each side of the centerline', 553 sq mi (1,430 km2)

ledger.note: 1979: the Canal Zone returns to Panama on 1 October. 'the Canal Zone ceased to exist on October 1, 1979, in compliance with provisions of the Torrijos–Carter Treaties' (signed 7 September 1977); 'The surrounding territory was returned first, in 1979' (Panama page). Thirty-five defence enclaves stayed American and the canal joint until 'Just after noon local time on December 31, 1999, all former Canal Zone parcels of all types had come under the exclusive jurisdiction of Panama'; that completion is not a second gain on the map.

wars.name: United States invasion of Panama
wars.outcome: No border moved. The Panama page gives only the dates: 'The United States invaded Panama on December 20, 1989' and 'The conflict ended on January 31, 1990.'
wars.note: Listed because it put foreign troops on Panamanian soil; the page says nothing of an occupation zone, so no occupation event is recorded.

certainty.note: The Canal Zone edge was a treaty line ('five miles (8 km) on each side of the centerline'). The pages opened give no dated treaty for Panama's land frontiers (page silent); the Darién frontier with Colombia runs through 'a nearly impenetrable jungle' and is the soft exception.

sources.title: Panama
sources.note: Identity, capital, infobox area 75,417 km2, independence from Colombia on 3 November 1903, 1977 treaties, the 1989 invasion. Silent on Coto and on land-frontier treaties.

sources.title: Panama Canal Zone
sources.note: The Zone created 18 November 1903, turned over 4 May 1904, abolished 1 October 1979, last parcels 31 December 1999; area 553 sq mi.

notes: BUDGET: two pages (Panama; Panama Canal Zone). ROW START: Cliopatria's Republic of Panama begins in 1905; the state begins 3 November 1903 (new keyframe 1903, same shape plus the future Zone). CANAL ZONE: Cliopatria returns it to Panama only in 2000 (5 cells, 1,285 km2); the pages say it ceased to exist on 1 October 1979, with US enclaves and joint canal operation until 31 December 1999, so the 1905 shape is adjusted to 1904-1978 and a 1979-1999 keyframe uses the 2000 outline. The united-states-of-america dossier carries the matching gain (1904) and loss (1979) with the same counterpart string. NOT OPENED (budget): the Coto War of 1921 and the White Award (the republic-of-costa-rica dossier carries 1921; Cliopatria's Panama shape does not change then) and Panama-Colombia frontier treaties. The Colombian-side split is in republic-of-colombia (1903). Rulers omitted: no list page opened. Region names used are all in the gazetteer (country Panama; Cliopatria shapes).
